key_insight: Cryogenic polarization-sensitive terahertz nanoscopy can directly isolate and map the bulk photovoltaic effect in bilayer graphene, linking photovoltaic response to quantum geometry and crystal symmetry.
engineering_relevance: This provides a new diagnostic tool for optimizing graphene-based optoelectronic devices by revealing how carrier density, temperature, and band structure affect nonlinear photocurrent generation.
method: Deep-subwavelength terahertz microscopy at cryogenic temperatures
Dual-gated AB bilayer graphene with polarization-dependent measurements
Compare spatially resolved photocurrent signatures against symmetry- and quantum-geometry-based theory
evidence_signal: The abstract reports enhanced optical conductivity and spatially resolved BPVE near resonance, with polarization-dependent twofold symmetry and agreement with theory across carrier density and temperature.
watch_item: The approach is specialized to cryogenic, dual-gated measurements and may be challenging to translate directly into practical room-temperature device workflows.
paper_title: Terahertz nanoscopy of quantum-geometric photovoltaics in bilayer graphene
